newsitem.title: UK: Montupet warns against strike in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: Montupet warns against strike in Belfast.

text.p: French car component firm Montupet S.A. warned on Thursday that its Northern Ireland plant near Belfast could close if an unofficial strike about pay and conditions is not settled on Friday.

Georges Senninger, managing director of Montupet UK Ltd, said the Amalgamated Engineering and Electrical Union (AEEU) had consistently opposed the strike and both the company and union wanted all employees to report for work on Friday morning.
"Management and the union will be at the factory gates to welcome our employees back to work," Senninger said in a statement to local media.
"If we do not seize this opportunity now, Montupet UK Ltd is at risk of closing their operations in Northern Ireland."
Some 280 of the 430 workforce are involved in the 11-day dispute at the plant at Dunmurry, in south Belfast, which makes alloy wheels and engine blocks.
Local newspapers said the workers had been told that Montupet was willing to negotiate a two year pay deal but only if work resumed.
"The unofficial action has been orchestrated by a small number of people who have exerted pressure on their colleagues," Senninger said.

He denied reports that two workers had been dismissed on April 14 but said that on Wednesday the company had issued "letters of dismissal for 20 employees who were involved in orchestrating and perpetuating this unofficial action."
